issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a method addGuestStudents(int, String) (an int plus a String reason), but the solution implementation defines addGuestStudents(int) with only a single int parameter. This mismatch between the specification and the provided solution can confuse students and cause incompatibilities with expected behavior or tests that rely on the two-parameter signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution match the specification by changing the solution's method signature to addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and (optionally) use the reason parameter (e.g., for logging or storing). Alternatively, if the intent was a single-parameter method, update the problem statement and UML to require addGuestStudents(int) so all artifacts are consistent.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a method addGuestStudents(int, String) (an int for new guest students and a String reason), but the solution implementation provides addGuestStudents(int) with only a single int parameter. This mismatch in the method signature for the same conceptual operation (adding guest students with an associated reason) creates a mapping confusion for students: they are instructed to implement/expect a two-parameter method but the provided solution uses a different identifier/signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across artifacts. Either (A) update the solution and template to implement addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) (and handle or store the reason appropriately), or (B) change the problem statement and UML to require addGuestStudents(int) if the reason is not needed. Prefer option A to match the current UML requirement.
